grh_cd3330e1657a36f5d79a.title: Writer's Block
paragraphs: Successful novelist Alex returns to his parents' home exhausted from publicity and hoping for quiet, only to be persuaded into leading a writing workshop he once attended. Most of the members spend more time performing the role of writer than actually writing, until newcomer Patience Webbersbee reads a sentimental children's story about a pigeon afraid of heights. Alex knows the story is poor but, attracted to Patience, softens his criticism while the group praises it. The dishonesty begins to trouble him so badly that he develops the writer's block of the title just as his relationship with Patience deepens. He finally tells her directly that the story is badly written and needs real work. Hurt, she leaves, but after rereading it objectively she returns and admits he was right. With honesty restored between them, Alex's block breaks and their romance resumes.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on August 2, 1979. It is listed as episode 129 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Cecily Tyson, David Downing, and Linda Kay Henning. Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, and Odie Hawkins as writer.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_cd70b9b12bee2a31758c.title: Its Always Tomorrow
paragraphs: American reporter Dave Sedgwick is sent to wartime England, where he meets Polly, a working-class waitress who distrusts patriotic slogans and the privileged people she serves. As Dave reports on factory workers, rationing, taxes and soldiers, he comes to see that many Britons are fighting not for empire but for a fairer postwar society. Dave and Polly fall in love, but she still refuses to romanticize the war. After a bombing badly wounds Dave, Polly agrees to leave her restaurant job for war work because she loves him, while insisting they must also fight to make sure ordinary people are not cheated after victory.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on January 2, 1945. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes William Quinn, Cathleen Cordell, John Stanley, and John Moore. Other credited names include Garnet Garrison as director, Martin Stern as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.5ab62c19ed82a8d9|Its Always Tomorrow]]. Robert St. John is credited as author and Martin Stern adapted it for radio.

grh_cd0efa3c689d39644abe.title: Ticket to Tangier
paragraphs: A personal advertisement lures broke Harry from Paris to Tangier, where Patsy admits she placed the notice and paid his fare. Her late husband was involved in heroin smuggling and left a large shipment hidden in an empty villa; Patsy wants Harry's contacts to sell it. An armed former associate arrives for the drugs, but Harry disarms him as police close in. Patsy flees and is later arrested for her husband's murder, while Harry retrieves the hidden bundle. Refusing to traffic the actual narcotics, he dumps the heroin into the Bay of Tangier and sells seven packages of confectioners' sugar to the waiting gangsters for $50,000, keeping only the prayer rug that had wrapped the shipment.

grh_cdc96fd15750dd733dcf.title: Story Of Windy The Truth Pills
paragraphs: Windy Smith's lifelong habit of telling outrageous stories makes him the easy suspect when money disappears from Clem Duke's store. Windy answers the accusation with an even wilder tale about armed gangsters, while Clem insists he must be guilty. Dr. Christian quietly turns the matter around with supposed truth pills that are nothing but sugar. Believing the medicine has forced honesty on him, Clem confesses that he took the money himself, lost it playing poker and blamed Windy because he was afraid to face his wife. Windy, who swallowed the same harmless pill, immediately launches into another impossible bandit story, proving that some habits are stronger than any imaginary cure.

grh_cd1fa86f2f02d8f4d205.title: Rocket Racket
paragraphs: Rocky answers an ad seeking an unattached man for dangerous experimental work and is recruited by a foundation supposedly preparing a revolutionary rocket flight. Snooping inside the ship, he finds painted canvas, studio props and dynamite instead of spacecraft equipment: the promoters have taken millions from a wealthy backer and plan to blow up the fake rocket with Rocky aboard. Rocky escapes by switching clothes with a guard and survives the explosion, then proves the fraud with debris from the phony craft.
